verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.1:2: Let it utterly vanish from the face of the earth, says the Lord;
verses.1:3: let man and livestock vanish; let the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea vanish. And the impious will grow weak, and I will remove the lawless from the face of the earth, says the Lord.
verses.1:4: And I will stretch out My hand against Judah and against all who dwell in Jerusalem; and I will remove from this place the names of Baal and the names of the priests,
verses.1:5: and those who worship the host of heaven on the rooftops, and those who worship and those who swear by the Lord, and those who swear by their king,
verses.1:6: and those who turn aside from the Lord, and those who do not seek the Lord, and those who do not hold fast to the Lord.
verses.1:7: Stand in awe before the presence of the Lord God, because the day of the Lord is near; for the Lord has prepared His sacrifice, He has consecrated His invited guests.
verses.1:8: And it will be on the day of the Lord's sacrifice that I will take vengeance on the rulers and on the house of the king and on all who are clothed in foreign garments;
verses.1:9: and I will openly take vengeance on the gateways on that day, those who fill the house of the Lord their God with impiety and deceit.
verses.1:10: And there will be on that day, says the Lord, the sound of an outcry from the gate of those who stab, and a wailing from the second, and a great crashing from the hills.
verses.1:11: Lament, you who dwell in the place that has been cut down, because all the people of Canaan have been made alike; all who are lifted up with silver have been utterly destroyed.
verses.1:12: And it will be on that day that I will search Jerusalem with a lamp, and I will take vengeance on the men who despise their observances; and as for those who say in their hearts, "The Lord will by no means do good, nor will He do harm,"
verses.1:13: their wealth will be for plunder, and their houses for desolation; and they will build houses and will by no means dwell in them, and they will plant vineyards and will by no means drink their wine.
verses.1:14: For the great day of the Lord is near, near and exceedingly swift; the sound of the day of the Lord has been appointed bitter and harsh, mighty.
verses.1:15: A day of wrath is that day, a day of affliction and distress, a day of untimely ruin and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist,
verses.1:16: a day of trumpet and outcry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
verses.1:17: And I will afflict human beings, and they will walk like the blind, because they sinned against the Lord; and He will pour out their blood like dust, and their flesh like dung;
verses.1:18: and their silver and their gold will by no means be able to rescue them on the day of the wrath of the Lord. And in the fire of His jealousy all the earth will be consumed, because He will bring about a complete end and haste upon all who dwell on the earth.
verses.2:1: Gather together and be bound together, you undisciplined nation,
verses.2:2: before you become like a flower passing away, before the wrath of the Lord comes upon you, before the day of the fury of the Lord comes upon you.
verses.2:3: Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth; practice justice and seek righteousness, and answer them, so that you may be sheltered on the day of the wrath of the Lord.
verses.2:4: For Gaza will be plundered, and Ashkelon will be for desolation, and Ashdod will be cast out at midday, and Ekron will be uprooted.
verses.2:5: Woe to you who dwell in the stretch of the sea, sojourners of the Cretans! The word of the Lord is against you, Canaan, land of foreigners, and I will destroy you from habitation;
verses.2:6: and Crete will become a pasture of flocks and a fold of sheep,
verses.2:7: and the stretch of the sea will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; upon them they will graze in the houses of Ashkelon, in the evening they will lodge from the presence of the sons of Judah, because the Lord their God has visited them and has turned back their captivity.
verses.2:8: I have heard the reproaches of Moab and the buffetings of the sons of Ammon, with which they reproached My people and magnified themselves against My borders.
verses.2:9: Therefore, as I live, says the Lord of powers, the God of Israel, surely Moab will be like Sodom, and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah, and Damascus abandoned like a heap of a threshing floor and made desolate forever; and the remnant of My people will plunder them, and the remnant of My nation will inherit them.
verses.2:10: This is for them in return for their arrogance, because they reproached and magnified themselves against the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:11: The Lord will appear against them, and He will utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth; and they will worship Him, each from his own place, all the islands of the nations.
verses.2:12: You also, Ethiopians, are the wounded of My sword;
verses.2:13: and He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy the Assyrian, and He will make Nineveh a waterless desolation like a wilderness;
verses.2:14: and flocks will graze in her midst, and all the wild beasts of the earth; and chameleons and hedgehogs will lie down in her paneled ceilings, and wild beasts will cry out in her breaches, ravens in her gateways, because cedar is her stature.
verses.2:15: This is the scornful city, who dwells in confidence, who says in her heart, "I am, and there is no one after me anymore." How she has become a desolation, a pasture of wild beasts! Everyone who passes through her will hiss and wave his hands.
verses.3:1: Alas, the illustrious and redeemed city,
verses.3:2: the dove! She did not heed a voice; she did not accept discipline; she did not trust in the Lord, and she did not draw near to her God.
verses.3:3: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like wolves of Arabia; they left nothing behind until the morning.
verses.3:4: Her prophets are spirit-driven, contemptuous men; her priests profane the holy things and act impiously toward the law.
verses.3:5: But the Lord is righteous in her midst and will by no means do wrong; morning by morning He will give His judgment to the light, and He was not hidden, and He did not know injustice in exaction, nor injustice to victory.
verses.3:6: In destruction I tore down the proud; their corner towers were made desolate. I will lay waste their roads completely so that no one passes through; their cities vanished because no one is present and no one dwells there.
verses.3:7: I said, "Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will by no means be utterly destroyed from her eyes, all that I avenged on her." Prepare yourself, rise early; all their gleaning has been ruined.
verses.3:8: Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising up for a testimony; because My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to take in kings, to pour out upon them all the wrath of My fury; because in the fire of My jealousy all the earth will be consumed.
verses.3:9: For then I will turn to peoples a tongue for its generation, so that all may call upon the name of the Lord, to serve Him under one yoke.
verses.3:10: From the ends of the rivers of Ethiopia I will accept among My dispersed ones; they will bring sacrifices to Me.
verses.3:11: On that day you will by no means be put to shame because of all your practices in which you acted impiously against Me; for then I will take away from you the scornful acts of your arrogance, and you will no longer continue to boast upon My holy mountain.
verses.3:12: And I will leave behind in you a gentle and humble people, and they will stand in awe of the name of the Lord,
verses.3:13: the remnant of Israel, and they will not do injustice and will not speak vain things, and a deceitful tongue will by no means be found in their mouth; because they themselves will graze and lie down, and there will be no one who terrifies them.
verses.3:14: Rejoice, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem! Be glad and delight yourself with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.3:15: The Lord has taken away your wrongdoings; He has redeemed you from the hand of your enemies. The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you will no longer see evil things.
verses.3:16: At that time the Lord will say to Jerusalem, "Take courage, Zion; do not let your hands grow slack."
verses.3:17: The Lord your God is in you; the Mighty One will save you. He will bring gladness upon you and renew you in His love, and He will be glad over you with delight as on a day of festival.
verses.3:18: And I will gather the crushed. Woe! Who took up a reproach against her?
verses.3:19: Look, I am acting in you for your sake at that time, says the Lord, and I will save her who has been oppressed and her who has been driven away; I will take them in for a boast and as renowned ones in all the earth.
verses.3:20: And they will be put to shame at that time when I do good to you, and at the time when I take you in; because I will make you renowned and a boast among all the peoples of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before you, says the Lord.

notes.1:4: Greek uses the feminine article with Baal ("the names of the [fem.] Baal"), reflecting the Septuagint convention of reading the feminine noun aischyne ("shame") in its place, and reads "names" where the Hebrew has "remnant."
notes.1:9: Greek reads "openly on the gateways" and "the house of the Lord their God," diverging from the Hebrew ("everyone who leaps over the threshold... the house of their master").
notes.1:10: Greek reads "the gate of those who stab" (apokentounton) where the Hebrew has "the Fish Gate."
notes.1:11: Greek translates the district name Maktesh as a participle ("the place that has been cut down") and renders the Hebrew verb as "have been made alike" (from homoioo) rather than "have been silenced/destroyed."
notes.1:12: Greek reads "who despise their observances" (ta phylagmata auton) rather than the Hebrew idiom "stagnant on their dregs," and has singular "a lamp."
notes.2:2: Greek reads "before you become like a flower passing away," differing from the Hebrew ("before the decree takes effect—the day passes like chaff").
notes.2:3: Greek renders "and answer them" (apokrinesthe auta), reading the Hebrew noun for "humility" from the homonymous root meaning "to answer."
notes.2:5: Greek names the coastal inhabitants "sojourners of the Cretans" (and "Crete" in 2:6) rather than the Hebrew "Cherethites," and renders Philistines with its standard term "foreigners" (allophyloi).
notes.2:9: Greek introduces the distinct proper name "Damascus" ("abandoned like a heap of a threshing floor"), where the Hebrew reads "a possession of nettles and a salt pit."
notes.2:14: Greek specifies "chameleons and hedgehogs" in the paneled ceilings, "ravens in her gateways," and "because cedar is her stature," diverging from the Hebrew fauna and architectural wording.
notes.3:1: Across 3:1-2, Greek reads "illustrious and redeemed city, the dove," construing the unvocalized Hebrew consonants from roots meaning "appear," "redeem," and "dove" rather than "rebellious, defiled, oppressing."
notes.3:3: Greek uses the distinct proper name "Arabia" ("wolves of Arabia"), reading the unvocalized Hebrew consonants for "evening" as "Arabia."
notes.3:5: Greek keeps the Lord as subject in the closing clauses ("He did not know injustice in exaction, nor injustice to victory"), whereas the Hebrew contrasts "the unjust [who] knows no shame."
notes.3:7: Greek reads "from her eyes" (rather than "her dwelling") and ends with "Prepare yourself, rise early; all their gleaning has been ruined," reading the Hebrew word for "deeds" as "gleanings."
notes.3:17: Greek reads "renew you in His love" (rather than "be quiet in His love") and closes the verse with "as on a day of festival," which opens 3:18 in the Hebrew; similarly, 3:20 opens with "And they will be put to shame" from the end of Hebrew 3:19.
